config.generalTabIntro: Dashboard-wide settings. Click Save to apply; the dashboard updates without a full reload.
config.colorsTabIntro:
Fine-tune dashboard and config colors here. Edit the default dark and light palettes, or create your own under Custom themes — then click Save colors to apply. Dozens of built-in themes are already available in General → Appearance if you want a ready-made look without editing every color.
Auto dark mode (General → Appearance) only works with built-in dark/light theme pairs — it is disabled when a custom theme is selected.

config.helpPageKeyboardIntro: Rebind search, navigation, and dashboard keys. The keyboard tab is not in the main tab bar — open it from the button below.
config.helpPageKeyboardItems:
• Open the cheat sheet on the dashboard with ! or F1. On first open (desktop), a one-time Got it balloon may appear beside the modal.
  • Bookmark grid: with a row selected, Home/End, Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End, and Page Up/Page Down move faster through bookmarks — see Help → Navigation.
  • Quick actions (row selected): Shift+M move to category or page; Shift+T quick-tag popover (Enter/Space toggles and advances); Shift+D delete with undo in the toast; plain Delete opens a confirmation dialog; closing Shift+M/Shift+T/Shift+D popovers restores keyboard highlight on the same row.
  • Config → Keyboard lists fixed add-bookmark defaults at the top: + / Ctrl+Shift+A (full modal), & (quick-add), and :new (command mode) — matching the cheat sheet.
  • On the dashboard (no input focused): + opens the full new-bookmark modal; & opens the quick-add omnibox; Ctrl+Shift+A opens the same full modal from anywhere.
  • Click Rebind next to any rebindable shortcut below the Bookmarks section, press your preferred key, then Save in the config header.
  • Enable Use shortcuts from all pages in General → Bookmarks — Behavior so keys work outside the dashboard.
  • Reset one shortcut or all bindings to defaults from the same screen.
  • Config tab bar (desktop): 1–9 jump to the Nth visible tab; ←/→ move to previous/next visible tab when focus is not in an input; S saves.
  • Config (desktop): Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — quick actions palette; Ctrl+Shift+K / Cmd+Shift+K — find any setting (see Help → General settings).

config.showHealthDashboardInfoMessage:
Controls visibility of the health beta entry in the dashboard header.

• On: shows a direct link to /health for issue triage and maintenance
• Off: hides the link, health page remains accessible by URL
config.showSearchFlowBannerInfoMessage:
Shows the small banner above the buttons that explains the main search flow.

• > opens search
• : opens commands
• ? opens finders
• × closes the banner; you can re-enable it here later
config.showWhatsNewHint: See a short summary of recent features — ℹ info buttons in config, Essentials/Advanced layers, dynamic PWA manifest, dashboard accessibility, and more.
config.interleaveModeInfoMessage:
Enabled:
• Press any letter to start fuzzy search (find bookmarks by name)
• Press '/' followed by letters to use shortcuts (e.g., /yt for YouTube)

Disabled:
• Press any letter to start shortcut search
• Press '/' followed by letters to use fuzzy search
config.packedColumnsInfoMessage:
When enabled, bookmark/category blocks are distributed round-robin across columns on wider screens.

• Reduces empty vertical gaps
• Can make reading order feel less top-to-bottom
• Saved instantly when toggled
config.showSyncToastsInfoMessage:
Show or hide cross-tab sync toasts.

• On: brief confirmation when another tab applies config/settings updates
• Off: no sync popup noise, but sync still happens
config.allowLocalBookmarksInfoMessage:
When enabled, bookmarks may use http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, and private LAN IPs. Status checks, link previews, auto-heal, and icon downloads from URLs can reach those hosts.

• On by default for local dev workflows
• Turn off if nextDash is exposed on a shared network (SSRF hardening)
config.globalShortcutsInfoMessage:
When enabled, shortcuts from every page can be used anywhere.

• Faster launch across pages
• Higher chance of shortcut conflicts if duplicates exist
config.showBookmarkStatusInfoMessage:
Two levels: this switch enables dashboard status globally. Each bookmark also needs its own status check under Config → Bookmarks.

• Useful for service links, but adds network checks
config.statusTwoLevelHint: Dashboard status is global. Each bookmark also needs its own status check enabled under Config → Bookmarks.
config.statusEssentialsHint: Per-bookmark checks (as in onboarding) live under Bookmarks. Health shows issues across all pages. Advanced: retries, colors, and ping.
config.statusEssentialsSummaryOnNone: On · no bookmarks with status checks yet
config.skipFastPingInfoMessage:
Changes how status checks run.

• Off: quick connectivity ping first, then HTTP check
• On: skip quick ping and run HTTP-only check
• Use if fast ping causes false negatives in your setup
config.statusOfflineRetriesInfoMessage:
How many failed ping attempts are needed before a bookmark is marked offline.

• Default: 3
• Range: 1–10
• Higher values reduce false alarms on flaky networks
config.statusOfflineRetryDelayInfoMessage:
Pause between retry pings within one status check.

• Default: 450 ms
• Range: 100–3000 ms
• Only applies while retries are still running
config.statusRecheckIntervalInfoMessage:
How often visible bookmarks are checked again in the background.

• Default: 5 minutes
• Shorter intervals use more network requests
config.backupsIntro: Back up and restore your entire dashboard — pages, categories, bookmarks, finders, settings, and custom themes. Use the ZIP backup to safeguard your data or move it to another device. Import browser bookmarks as a starting point, or export all bookmarks to CSV for use in spreadsheet tools.
config.backupsBrowserImportHint: Export bookmarks from Chrome, Firefox, or Edge as HTML and import here. Folders become categories; duplicate URLs are skipped. Missing icons are fetched automatically with a progress bar.
config.backupsCsvExportHint: Downloads all bookmarks from all pages as a single CSV file (name, URL, category, page, shortcut, tags, notes). Opens in Excel, Google Sheets, or any text editor.
config.backupInfo: Downloads a ZIP with bookmarks, pages, categories, finders, settings, custom themes (colors.json), uploaded dashboard favicon/font, and bookmark icon files (data/icons/).
config.backupError: Failed to create backup. Please try again.
config.importInfo:
Select a ZIP exported from nextDash to restore bookmarks, pages, categories, finders, settings, themes, branding uploads, and icon files. This replaces your current data.

Bookmark URL rules use allowLocalBookmarks from the imported settings.json when that file is in the ZIP.

Important: Do not modify or rename files inside the ZIP, as this may cause import errors.
config.importSuccess: Data imported successfully! The page will reload.
config.importSuccessSkipped: Import completed. {count} bookmark(s) with disallowed URLs were skipped.
config.importError: Failed to import data. Please try again.
config.importInvalidFile: Invalid file. Please select a valid nextDash backup ZIP file.
config.importConfirmMessage: This will replace all your current bookmarks, pages, categories, finders, settings, themes, branding uploads, and icon files with the data from the selected ZIP. This action cannot be undone. Continue?
config.browserImportNoNew: All URLs from this file already exist on the selected page — nothing to import.
config.browserImportInvalidFile: Please select a browser bookmark HTML export file.
config.browserImportEmpty: No valid bookmarks found in the file.
config.csvExportError: Failed to export bookmarks to CSV.
config.browserImportModalUnavailable: Could not open the import dialog. Refresh the page and try again.
config.settingsExportHint: Downloads your current settings as JSON. Does not include bookmarks, pages, or themes.
config.settingsImportHint: Overwrites current settings with a previously exported JSON file.
config.settingsImportInvalidFile: Please select a valid settings JSON file.
config.settingsImportConfirmMessage: This will overwrite your current settings. Continue?
config.fuzzySuggestionsStartWith: Only show suggestions that start with the query
config.fuzzySuggestionsInfoMessage:
When enabled, shows additional bookmark suggestions in shortcut search that contain the typed letters anywhere in their name.

For example:
• Typing 'ho' will show bookmarks like 'HomePage', 'PhotoShop', etc.
• Works alongside existing shortcut matches
• Can be further filtered with the sub-option below
config.includeFindersInSearchInfoMessage:
When enabled, you can access finders directly from the main search.

• Type a finder shortcut (e.g., "YT") and press space to automatically switch to finder mode.
• If a bookmark has the same shortcut as a finder, both options will appear for selection.
config.keepSearchOpenWhenEmptyInfoMessage:
When enabled, the search UI stays open even with an empty query.

• Good for keyboard-only workflows
• Can feel busier if you prefer a minimal idle state
config.showTagCloudButtonInfoMessage: Shows a / button stacked with What's new (desktop). Press / or click to open a tag word cloud (larger = more used). Click or Enter/Space toggles tags in the filter — the modal stays open so you can combine several. Bookmarks match any selected tag (OR). Active tags appear as chips under the title (each with ×) and on the / FAB (#work +1 when multiple). Arrow keys move between tags and Clear tag filter. Escape in the cloud closes the modal; Escape on the dashboard clears all filters. Clear tag filter removes every tag. • Related: :tag work in command mode lists bookmarks in the palette without changing the dashboard • Desktop / wide layout only — hidden on mobile • On by default (desktop only) • Turn off here to hide the button and modal entirely
config.showTipsInfoMessage:
Shows rotating shortcut/help tips above action buttons.

• Helpful for onboarding and reminding advanced shortcuts
• Turn off for a cleaner footer
config.showPageTabsInfoMessage:
Controls whether page navigation tabs are visible.

• On: click/tap tabs to switch pages
• Off: switch pages using keyboard shortcuts only
config.showPageNamesInTabsInfoMessage:
Controls tab labels when tabs are visible.

• On: show page names
• Off: show page numbers
config.hideEmptyCategoriesInfoMessage:
When enabled, categories with no bookmarks are hidden on the dashboard.

• Keeps the dashboard tidy
• Empty categories are still visible in config → categories
config.alwaysCollapseCategoriesInfoMessage:
When enabled, categories start collapsed when dashboard data loads.

• Cleaner first view
• Requires extra clicks to open content each session

config.resetOnboardingSuccess: Onboarding reset. Open the dashboard to start the wizard.

config.configBookmarksTourWelcomeBody: List on the left, detail editor on the right. Structure workspace above stays collapsed until you need pages or categories.
config.configBookmarksTourListControlsBody: Pick page and category, change sort, search below, and use + Bookmark for Add & edit (needs Save) or Quick add (⚡, saves immediately).
config.configBookmarksTourStructureBody: Use the structure columns to add or reorder pages and categories, or jump straight to a bookmark.
config.configBookmarksTourPageFilterBody: Choose which dashboard page you edit. Filter by category or change sort order in large collections.
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentStepBody: Optional: we add temporary demo bookmarks, then remove them before you finish.
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentMessage: We add a couple of temporary bookmarks with random public websites, then remove them before you finish the tour.
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentYesBody: Great — we use random public sites as examples. First: a bookmark in the list and editor (not saved to disk until you click Save).
config.configBookmarksTourDemoConsentNoBody: Skipped the live demos. Open + Bookmark anytime for Add & edit or Quick add (⚡).
config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoIntroBody: Open + Bookmark → Add & edit. It adds a row and opens the editor — click Save when you are done.
config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoDoneBody: Edit name, URL, category, and more on the right. This demo row stays in the editor until you click Save — it is not on the dashboard yet.
config.configBookmarksTourEditorDemoFailBody: Open + Bookmark → Add & edit to create a bookmark, then fill name and URL on the right.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddBody: Quick add (⚡) saves immediately — unlike Add & edit, no Save click needed.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddDoneBody: Quick add writes straight to disk — no Save click. The bookmark appears in the list and on the dashboard.
config.configBookmarksTourQuickAddFailBody: Open + Bookmark → Quick add (⚡) to add a bookmark that saves immediately.
config.configBookmarksTourEditorBody: Edit name, URL, shortcut, category, tags, pin, and status. Fetch favicon and link previews here.
config.configBookmarksTourModalOpenIntroBody: Quick add (⚡) opens the same bookmark modal as the dashboard + button.
config.configBookmarksTourModalOpenDoneBody: Quick add uses the same + modal as the dashboard. Name and URL are prefilled — Create saves immediately to this page.
config.configBookmarksTourModalOpenFailBody: Click Quick add (⚡) to open the + bookmark modal.
config.configBookmarksTourModalWizardIntroBody: The tour card stays at the bottom; the + modal stays in the center so you can use both.
config.configBookmarksTourModalWizardBody: On small screens the + modal is a short wizard: URL first, then name and options.
config.configBookmarksTourModalDesktopBody: On desktop you see the full form at once. The tour card stays beside the modal so fields stay readable.
config.configBookmarksTourModalSaveIntroBody: Creating here writes the bookmark to disk immediately — no Config Save click needed.
config.configBookmarksTourModalSaveDoneBody: That bookmark was saved straight to disk (unlike editor-only changes). It appears in the list and on the dashboard.
config.configBookmarksTourModalSaveFailBody: The demo could not be saved automatically — you can create one with Quick add (⚡) yourself.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardIntroBody: The dashboard toolbar + button opens this modal too. We visit the dashboard next.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardHandoffBody: Next we open the dashboard briefly: the + toolbar button uses this same modal. Click Next to continue there, then you return here to clean up.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardToolbarBody: Press + or click this button to add a bookmark without opening Config.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardModalBody: Same form as in Config Quick add. We prefilled another random site for this step.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardCreateIntroB: Creating here saves immediately and shows the tile on your current page.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardTileBody: Here is the new tour bookmark on your dashboard. It is removed when you finish the tour in Config.
config.configBookmarksTourDashboardReturnBody: Click Next to return to Config → Bookmarks and remove all demo bookmarks.
config.configBookmarksTourSearchBody: Filter the bookmark list by name or URL. Clear the field to show everything again.
config.configBookmarksTourBulkBody: Select multiple bookmarks, then use Move to for page or category changes, plus pin, status, favicon refresh, or delete.
config.configBookmarksTourBulkDemoBody: We selected a few bookmarks so you can try Move to, pin, status, favicon refresh, or delete.
config.configBookmarksTourBulkEmptyBody: Select bookmarks with the checkboxes in the list to show bulk actions.
config.configBookmarksTourFaviconBody: Choose when bookmark icons refresh: on save or only manually.
config.configBookmarksTourSaveBody: Add & edit changes are not written until you click Save. Unsaved edits are highlighted.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupIntroBody: Remove temporary tour bookmarks from the editor and saved data.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupResumeBody: Welcome back — remove the temporary tour bookmarks from your library.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupConfirmMessage: We remove the temporary tour bookmarks from the editor and from the saved page so your library stays unchanged.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupDoneBody: All tour bookmarks are removed. Your collection is back to how it was before the tour.
config.configBookmarksTourCleanupKeptBody: Demo bookmarks may still be present. Delete them in the list or restart the tour from General → System tools.

config.resetConfigFindersTourFailedTab: Could not start the Finders tour. Open the Finders tab first.

config.resetConfigFindersTourFailedMobile: Could not start the Finders tour. Use a wider window or turn off mobile device emulation in your browser.
config.configFindersTourWelcomeBody: Finders are quick-search shortcuts to external sites — Google, DuckDuckGo, Wikipedia, and more. You trigger them from the dashboard with ? plus a shortcut key.
config.configFindersTourConceptBody: Each finder has a name, a search URL with %s as the placeholder for your query, and a one-letter shortcut. nextDash opens the finished URL in your browser — it does not search inside your bookmark list.
config.configFindersTourFieldsBody: Edit each row here: display name, full search URL (must include %s), lowercase shortcut (a–z), and optional comma-separated tags for filtering in config.
config.configFindersTourAddBody: Click + Add finder for a blank row. Change the URL and shortcut to match any search site you use regularly.
config.configFindersTourGoogleIntroBody: A common pattern is Google with URL https://www.google.com/search?q=%s. We prefer shortcut {preferred} if it is free; otherwise we suggest the next available letter. Next we can add this row — only if you agree.
config.configFindersTourGoogleConsentShortcutNo: Shortcut {preferred} is already used by another finder — we will use {shortcut} for this Google example instead.
config.configFindersTourGoogleConsentBody:
We can add a ready-made Google finder to your list now:

• Name: Google
• URL: https://www.google.com/search?q=%s
• Shortcut: {shortcut}

You still need to click Save in config to keep it. Nothing is sent to Google until you use the finder on the dashboard.
config.configFindersTourGoogleNoShortcut: All single-letter shortcuts are already used by finders. Free a letter or remove a finder, then try the tour again.
config.configFindersTourGoogleShortcutTaken: Shortcut {shortcut} was just taken by another finder. Pick a different shortcut manually.
config.configFindersTourGoogleAddedBody: Here is your Google finder. The URL uses %s where your search words go. On the dashboard, press ? then {shortcut} and your query — for example ?{shortcut} nextdash opens Google with that search.
config.configFindersTourGoogleSkippedBody: No problem — you can add finders yourself with + Add finder. Use %s in the URL where the search text should go, and pick a single-letter shortcut.
config.configFindersTourUsageBody: Press ? to open finder mode. Type {shortcut} and your words — e.g. ?{shortcut} nextdash — then Enter. The %s in the URL is replaced with your query. Enable “Include finders in search” under General → Advanced if you also want finders in normal search results.
config.configFindersTourMaintainBody: Drag the ⠿ handle to change order. Remove deletes after confirmation. Usage stats (uses · last used) help you see which finders you actually use.
config.configFindersTourSaveBody: Finder changes are stored when you click Save. If you added the Google example during this tour, save now to keep it after a refresh.

config.resetConfigStatsTourFailed: Could not start the Stats tour. Open the Stats tab first.
config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedTab: Could not start the Stats tour. Open the Stats tab first.
config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedDom: Could not start the Stats tour. Stats are still loading — refresh the page and try again.

config.resetConfigStatsTourFailedMobile: Could not start the Stats tour. Use a wider window or disable mobile device emulation in your browser.
config.configStatsTourWelcomeBody: Below the intro line, this is your stats dashboard: quick links on the left and insight sections on the right. Everything here is read-only — after you save bookmarks or settings elsewhere, reopen this tab to refresh the numbers.
config.configStatsTourIndexBody: Use the quick links on the left to scroll to any block. On wide screens the index stays visible while you read the charts and tables on the right.
config.configStatsTourOverviewBody: Counts for pages, categories, bookmarks, URLs, and shortcuts — plus average opens per bookmark. Click ℹ for a short explanation of each metric.
config.configStatsTourScoreBody: A 0–100 health score with a colour bar. The list below explains penalties: never-opened bookmarks, stale items, duplicate URLs, shortcut conflicts, and more.
config.configStatsTourActivityBody: Lifetime opens for bookmarks active in the period, a count of active bookmarks, and a sparkline of when bookmarks were last opened (not individual opens). Switch week, month, 3 months, 6 months, or all time.
config.configStatsTourTopBody: Tables for most opened and most recently opened bookmarks, with page names and timestamps. Change the period filter to focus on recent usage or all-time leaders.
config.configStatsTourPagesBody: Compare bookmark counts and opens per page, then per category within pages. Use period buttons to limit stats to recent activity or view all time.
config.configStatsTourTagsBody: See tag coverage, unique tags, and which tags appear on the most bookmarks. Tables rank tags and the most opened tagged bookmarks.
config.configStatsTourShortcutsBody: See how many bookmarks have keyboard shortcuts and which shortcuts get the most opens — useful when tuning your search workflow.
config.configStatsTourRotBody: Find bookmarks you never opened, items stale in the chosen period, and recently added links. Tables list candidates to review or remove.
config.configStatsTourConflictsBody: Duplicate URLs and shortcut conflicts are counted here with detail rows. Open Health for deeper triage and one-click fixes on the dashboard.
config.configStatsTourSearchBody: Shows whether the search index is built and how status monitoring is configured. Reopen this tab after changing settings or bookmarks to see updated numbers.
config.configCategoriesTourWelcomeBody: Categories are the columns on your dashboard. Each page has its own list — pick a page, add or rename categories, drag to reorder, and remove ones you no longer need.
config.configCategoriesTourPageBody: Use the Page menu to edit categories for that dashboard page. Switch pages here without leaving the Categories tab.
config.configCategoriesTourAddBody: Click + Add category for a new row. Next we can add a temporary “news” category for practice — only if you agree.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoIntroBody: A short demo helps you see how categories appear on the dashboard. We can create “news” on this page now.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoConsentMessage: For this tour we add a temporary category named “news” on the current page. You will reorder it and remove it before the tour ends — nothing stays on your dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoAddedBody: Here is your “news” category. Change the name or emoticon anytime. Column order here matches the category tabs on the dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourDemoSkippedBody: No demo category was added. Use + Add category when you are ready — you can still follow the rest of the tour.
config.configCategoriesTourFieldsBody: Edit the display name and optional two-character emoticon. The category id stays stable when you rename — bookmarks keep their link.
config.configCategoriesTourReorderIntroBody: Drag the ⠿ handle to change order. Next we move “news” to the first slot so you can see the tab shift on the dashboard.
config.configCategoriesTourReorderDoneBody: We moved “news” to the first position — check your dashboard: the category tab order follows this list. Drag the ⠿ handle anytime to change order yourself.
config.configCategoriesTourRemoveBody: Click Remove (red) on a row to delete that category. You confirm in a dialog; bookmarks can be moved, uncategorized, or deleted depending on your choice.

config.configCollectionsTourLogicBody: AND requires every rule to match; OR includes bookmarks that match any rule. The demo uses OR so tag, category, or shortcut matches are enough.

• On first launch, a short guided setup helps configure the dashboard in minutes.
  • You can choose language, link behavior, weather/date, classic, modern, or glass layout, search mode, smart collections, optional status monitoring across all pages (up to 10 shown; GitHub is highlighted), and a combined keyboard & mouse bookmark step.

config.helpPageNavigationItems:
• Switch pages with number keys 1-9 (not while the search overlay is open); the first visible bookmark on the new page is selected automatically.
  • On the page tab strip, use ←/→/Home/End when a tab is focused; Enter or Space activates the tab.
  • Move between pages with Shift + Left/Right — plain ←/→ move bookmarks, not pages.
  • Cmd+C (Mac) copies the selected bookmark URL when a row is highlighted.
  • Start grid navigation with Tab (first bookmark is in the Tab order even before arrow keys), a bookmark click, G then 1–9 / GG, or the first arrow key; then Up/Down and Left/Right move the selection.
  • Collapsed categories and launcher tiles dimmed by search are skipped by keyboard navigation. Focus a category header and press Enter or Space to toggle collapse.
  • When you move the mouse over bookmarks, the stale keyboard highlight softens until your next keyboard move.
  • Press Tab / Shift+Tab to step linearly through bookmarks when one is selected; at the first/last bookmark, Tab exits to the header/FAB.
  • Press G then a digit 1–9 or hold G (~300 ms) to jump to the nth visible category or smart collection and select its first bookmark; G+P jumps to the first pinned bookmark; GG (second G while the chord is pending) jumps to the very first bookmark. A quick tap on G opens bookmark shortcuts that start with G instead.
  • Grid navigation (bookmark selected): Home / End — first/last bookmark in the current category; Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End — first/last on the page; Page Up / Page Down — jump about one screen.
  • Open selected bookmark with Enter or Space.
  • Clear keyboard selection with Esc — focus moves to the first bookmark (also undoes the latest drag reorder when applicable).
  • Shift+M quick-move to another category or page; Shift+D quick-delete with undo in the toast.
  • Page overview (,): ↑/↓ or Tab; Enter or Space switches page; focus stays inside the panel.

  • Recent bookmarks — phone: command mode :open recent (or * with an external keyboard). Desktop: Recent footer button or *.

  • Tag word cloud (/) — desktop only. On phone, filter with :tag in command mode or tag: in search.
  • Header — phone: Pages overview sheet and Config link; page tab strip, health badge, launcher, What's new, and tag cloud FAB are hidden.
  • Config — phone: General (language, theme basics, layout) and Help only — theme colours are view-only; structure tabs (bookmarks, pages, categories, tags, collections, …) need a wider screen. Desktop: full editor, backups, stats, theme editor, guided tours, and all settings.
  • Touch: long-press a bookmark row for inline edit; swipe between pages when enabled. Hover link previews and guided tours are desktop-width only.
config.helpPageBookmarksDashboardItems:
• Smart collections: inline edit and delete from smart-collection rows update the canonical bookmark on the page — tags and notes stay in sync across columns.
  • While inline edit is open: keyboard grid navigation and page-switch keys are paused; swipe and Ctrl+V quick-add paste are blocked. Cancelling inline edit restores focus to the bookmark row.
  • Keyboard: arrow keys move the highlight; Tab / Shift+Tab steps linearly through bookmarks when one is selected (at the grid edge, Tab exits to header/FAB); hold G or G + digit jumps to the nth visible category or smart collection (quick tap G opens shortcuts starting with G); ; (semicolon) opens inline edit on the highlighted row; Home/End and Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End jump within category or page (see Navigation).
  • Quick actions (row selected): Shift+M move to category or page; Shift+T quick-tag popover (Enter/Space toggles and advances); Shift+D delete with undo in the toast (popover); plain Delete opens a confirmation dialog; closing those popovers restores keyboard highlight on the same bookmark row.
    • lter bulk actions: when filtering by tags, use the toolbar under the chips to open tabs, copy links, move, or delete all matches on the page.
  • Desktop discoverability promos: one-time Got it balloons beside features (search modes, filters, grid navigation, tag cloud, bulk toolbar, recent modal, preview, quick-add, week overview, category collapse, quick move/delete, page overview). Hidden on mobile.
  • Accessibility: the bookmark area uses role="grid" with labelled category headers; the cheat sheet (!) lists all navigation keys and opens with focus in the filter box.
  • Inline edit field labels match Config → Bookmarks (name, URL, tags, pin, status check, save/delete).
  • Quick-add (&): press & anywhere on the dashboard (when no input is focused) to open the quick-add omnibox at the bottom — type name | url | shortcut in one field and press Enter. Favicon is fetched automatically.
  • New-bookmark modal (+ / Ctrl+Shift+A): press + on the dashboard or Ctrl+Shift+A anywhere (when no input is focused) to open the full add-bookmark form with page, category, preview, and more options.
  • Paste to quick-add (Ctrl+V): paste a URL to open the new-bookmark modal pre-filled with that URL. Works when no input is focused and search is not active.
  • Mouse — left strip: the narrow drag handle on the left of each row is for dragging: reorder inside a category or drop into another category column.
  • Mouse — long-press: press and hold about half a second on the bookmark row (not on the drag strip) to open the same inline edit form.
  • Hover: when Link Preview Cards are enabled, hovering a bookmark shows a rich preview card (title/description/image/domain). You can disable cards or tune hover delay (100/150/250 ms) in config#general → Dashboard.
  • Tag cloud (/, desktop): when enabled, opens a modal to filter dashboard tiles by tag. Click or Enter/Space toggles tags (modal stays open); bookmarks match any selected tag (OR). Active tags show as header chips. Bulk actions appear in the toolbar when matches exist. Escape on the dashboard clears all filters; Escape in the cloud closes the modal only.
config.helpPageSearchItems:
• > open normal search, : commands, ? finders.
  • Command palette (:): lone : shows 10 collapsible groups (add & remove, edit, open & inspect, search, navigation, layout, display, smart collections, tag filter, system) — click a header to expand. Toggle and view commands keep the palette open after Enter; rows refresh with (on)/(off), ✓, or a brief flash.
  • Bookmark actions: :move, :edit, :copy, :category / :cat, :page, :open pinned / tag / category. Navigation: :recent (*), :overview (,), :cheat, :add (&), :config, :reload, :goto config / stats / health. Display: :dark, :title, :lang, :animations, :status, :opacity, :collections. Tools: :backup, :export (ZIP), :metadata, :tour, :promo, :filter / :filter clear; :find clear removes in-page filter; :health page [n] filters health by page.
  • On desktop, the highlighted search match receives keyboard focus; closing search restores focus to the opener.
  • Launcher keys (>, :, ?, +, &) are ignored while a modal, page overview, inline edit, tag cloud, or date popover is open.
  • Page keys 1–9 and Shift+←/→ do not change pages while the search overlay is active.
  • Empty overlay: recent searches and recent commands show as chips — highlight the chip row with ↑/↓, then ←/→ cycle chips and Enter applies. Mode tabs at the top switch input mode on click.
  • & open the quick-add omnibox — type name | url | shortcut and press Enter to add a bookmark without leaving the dashboard.
  • + (dashboard) or Ctrl+Shift+A (anywhere) open the full new-bookmark modal.
  • / on the dashboard with Tag cloud (/) enabled (desktop): opens the tag word cloud — toggle one or more tags (OR match) while the modal stays open. Otherwise, or inside the search overlay, / follows your fuzzy/interleave search setting.
  • :tag lists tags in command mode; :tag work or :tag:work shows matching bookmarks in the palette only (dashboard stays complete). :tag +name / :tag -name add or remove a tag on the keyboard-selected bookmark.
  • :layoutversion modern / classic / glass / toggle switch layout version (classic → modern → glass) (not the same as :layout presets). Use :layout, :density, and :buttons for other quick UI changes.
  • :history — browse recent searches from the command bar; :history clear wipes all history. Or open search with an empty query and hover a history row to × delete individual entries.
  • :duplicate / :duplicates — scan for duplicate URLs across all pages (opens Health duplicates view).
  • Filter autocomplete: expand Filters in the empty state or start with category:, status:, page:, or tag: and pick a suggestion — one expandable Filters group only.
  • Partial filter values (e.g. status:on) keep showing autocomplete until the token is complete.
  • Bookmark shortcuts starting with G: a quick tap opens the shortcut search bar; hold G or press G then a digit without opening search activates category jump instead.
  • tag: in > search filters results in the overlay — e.g. tag:work shows bookmarks whose tags include work (partial match).
  • status: values: online, offline, checked, unchecked, pinned, unpinned, broken, ok — online/offline use persisted reachability on monitored bookmarks.
  • page: values: current, all, or a page number like page:2.
  • Turn on "Keep search open when empty" for fast repeated searches.
config.helpPageDateWeatherItems:
• Toggle date and time independently, and choose date format: short slash, short dash, MM/DD/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD, weekday only, or long weekday.
  • Choose time format: 24-hour or 12-hour AM/PM.
  • Date/time render on one line as 13:35 @ 30-04-2026; weather renders on the next line.
  • Weather line includes a small icon per condition (clear/cloudy/rain/snow/fog/drizzle/thunderstorm/unknown).
  • Enable weather display and select location source (browser or manual city).
  • Set Celsius/Fahrenheit and weather refresh interval from the Date & Weather card in general settings.
  • If weather does not show, verify manual location text and save once.
config.helpPageSmartItems:
• Today, Recently opened, Stale bookmarks, and Most used are built-in smart collections.
  • Each can be enabled/disabled independently and limited to specific pages.
  • Set item limit to 0 for unlimited.
  • Enable Tag collections in config → general → Smart Collections to auto-generate one collection per tag.
  • Set a minimum bookmark count to filter out rarely-used tags.
  • Smart sections support collapse/expand on the dashboard.
config.helpPageTagsItems:
• Add comma-separated tags to any bookmark in config → bookmarks or via the inline editor on the dashboard.
  • Tags are normalized: trimmed, lowercased, and deduplicated on save.
  • Search (>): tag:work filters matches in the search overlay — partial tag names supported; does not change the dashboard layout.
  • Dashboard tag cloud (desktop): enable Tag cloud (/) in config → general → Header & Buttons. Press / or click the / FAB for a word cloud (size = usage). Click or Enter/Space toggles tags in the filter — the modal stays open so you can combine several. Bookmarks match any selected tag (OR). Active tags show as chips in the header bar (each with its own remove) and on the / FAB (#work +1 when multiple). Escape on the dashboard clears all filters and returns focus to bookmarks; Escape in the cloud closes the modal only. Clear tag filter removes every tag. Arrow keys move between tags and the clear button.
  • Command palette (:): :tag lists all tags; :tag work or :tag:work lists bookmarks with that tag inside the palette only. :tag +work / :tag -work add or remove a tag on the keyboard-selected bookmark.
  • Config → tags (desktop): global management across all pages — filterable tag cloud and list; expand a row for bookmarks with page name, Open (correct page), and − tag; Rename merges when the name already exists; Search opens Bookmarks with tag: filter. Changes auto-save with undo (cross-page safe). ↑/↓ on a focused row moves between tags. Not on phone — structure tabs need a wider screen.
  • Enable Tag collections in config → general to automatically show one dashboard group per tag.
  • Tags guided tour: first visit on a desktop-width window — tag cloud, list actions, optional demo bookmark with tag tour-demo (consent), then cleanup. Replay: Advanced → System & tools → Show Tags tour again.
config.helpPageCollectionsItems:
• Create dynamic bookmark groups in config → collections.
  • Each collection has a name, optional icon (emoji), match logic (AND/OR), and one or more rules.
  • Rule fields: tag, category, or shortcut. Operators: includes or excludes.
  • AND: all rules must match. OR: at least one rule must match.
  • Collections appear as groups on the dashboard alongside smart collections.
  • Changes save immediately — no need to press the main Save button.
  • Tag collections (auto-generated per tag) and custom collections are shown before regular categories on the dashboard.
  • Collections guided tour: optional demo collection with tag/category/shortcut rules, save to dashboard, preview, cleanup. Replay: System & tools → Show Collections tour again.
config.helpPageSortingItems:
• Pinned bookmarks always stay on top of non-pinned bookmarks.
  • Pinned state is shown with a compact pin icon on dashboard rows.
  • Pinned bookmarks are always sorted alphabetically.
  • Non-pinned bookmarks use your selected sort mode (manual, A-Z, recent, pinned-first behavior).
  • Categories can be collapsed and can default to collapsed.
  • Drag the grip handle (⠿) that appears when hovering a category title to reorder categories directly on the dashboard — the new order is saved automatically.
  • Category order in config → categories (desktop): drag rows or focus a row and press ↑/↓ — order auto-saves (~600 ms). Each row shows a bookmark count; merge previews how many will move.
  • Categories guided tour: per-page list, add category, optional demo news category, reorder hint, remove, cleanup. Replay: System & tools → Show Categories tour again.
config.helpPageManageItems:
• Use the config workspace to manage pages, categories, and bookmarks in one place.
  • Two shortcuts (desktop): Ctrl+Shift+K / Cmd+Shift+K — find any setting, tab, or help section; Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — run quick actions (new page, bookmark, refresh favicons). One mental model: search navigates, palette acts.
  • Pages guided tour: list, add page, optional demo page, dashboard handoff, remove, cleanup. Replay: System & tools → Show Pages tour again.
  • Config → pages (desktop): drag or ↑/↓ reorders with auto-save (~600 ms); Archive hides a page without deleting bookmarks; remove/archive use stable ids (safe after reorder). Create pages with templates or quick actions via Ctrl+K/Cmd+K.
  • Config → categories (desktop): per-page list; changing the page selector saves pending order/names/icons first; remove and merge use category id (not list position).
  • The Bookmarks tab uses a split-view layout: compact list left, detail panel right. Edit all fields: name, URL, page, category, shortcut, icon, tags, note, pinned, and status check.
  • Bookmarks guided tour: extended spotlight tour on a desktop-width window — structure, filters, optional demo bookmarks (editor, + modal, dashboard +), search, bulk toolbar, favicon policy, cleanup, Save. Replay: System & tools → Show Bookmarks tour again.
  • Stats guided tour: read-only insights across all stats sections (overview, score, activity, conflicts link to Health). Replay: Show Stats tour again.
  • Add comma-separated tags in the detail panel or inline editor — saved normalized (trimmed, lowercase).
  • Bookmarks support favicon fetch from URL (auto on URL blur or manual via Fetch favicon).
  • Set icons via upload or icon URL in the detail panel.
  • Bulk actions: select rows, move category or page, toggle pin, delete, and bulk refresh favicons.
  • Use Alt+Up / Alt+Down to reorder quickly within the list.
config.helpPageFindersItems:
• Format: ?shortcut your query (example: ?du linux for the default DuckDuckGo finder).
  • Use %s in the search URL where the query is inserted (e.g. https://www.google.com/search?q=%s).
  • Config → finders (desktop): drag or ↑/↓ reorders with auto-save (~600 ms); filter the list; usage stats refresh when you open the tab. Duplicate shortcuts are highlighted; save is blocked until resolved.
  • If a bookmark and finder share a shortcut, both options appear in search when Include finders in search is enabled.
  • Finders guided tour: first visit on a desktop-width window — 8 steps; optional Google example after consent. Replay: Advanced → System & tools → Show Finders tour again.
config.helpPageStatusItems:
• Enable status checks to display online/offline state.
  • Optionally show ping and loading indicators.
  • Use "Skip fast ping check" to reduce noise and speed up checks.
  • Open /health for issue triage: ping broken links, run repair actions from the overflow menu (archive, detect redirect, refresh title), and delete bookmarks directly from Health.
  • Preview cards and metadata refresh settings are documented in config help sections.
config.helpPageHealthItems:
• Visit the health beta page (dashboard header or /health) to triage bookmarks across all pages.
  • Nine summary stat cards on one row — click to filter (broken, duplicate, stale, etc.). First visit defaults to broken.
  • Compact controls — search, page filter, status pills, and bulk buttons (retest all checked, open broken, merge duplicates) in one panel.
  • Multi-select — check rows, select all visible, bulk refresh favicons, or bulk delete (with confirm).
  • Open in Config — click a row or press Enter to edit the bookmark in Config → Bookmarks.
  • Per-row favicon, health score, and config-style actions: open URL, dashboard link, re-check status, favicon refresh, overflow repair menu (Status → re-check status; detect redirect, refresh title, archive, delete) — styled per Classic / Modern / Glass layout (rounded chips; glass blur in glass mode).
  • Action runtime — health-runtime.js coalesces re-renders, blocks concurrent row actions, and times out slow API calls so repairs do not freeze the page.
  • Detect redirect — uses a fast redirect-only suggest (redirectOnly=1); confirm shows the proposed URL; errors surface in the status bar.
  • Layout parity — health uses the same layout version and visual settings as the dashboard (preset, density, custom background, opacity, font weight, animations, auto dark mode); saves in config apply live.
  • Keyboard — j/k or arrows move focus; O opens the URL.
  • Filter, sort, search, and page state persist in the session and sync to URL query parameters.
config.helpPageTipsItems:
• Tips rotate every 5 to 8 seconds.
  • After every 5 normal tips, a priority tip is shown.
  • Priority tips include recent, cheatsheet, ; inline edit, left-strip drag hint, navigation, and + for the full add-bookmark form.
  • Normal tips also mention keyboard rebinding — see Help → Keyboard shortcuts.
  • The + modal lets you set name, URL, page, category, shortcut, icon (URL or upload), and a note when creating a bookmark.
  • You can toggle tips in config#general under Dashboard.
config.helpPageBackupItems:
• Backup & restore is in config → backups.
  • From the dashboard: :backup opens config backups; :export downloads a ZIP backup immediately.
  • ZIP backup exports pages, bookmarks (including tags), categories, finders (finders.json), settings (including collections), and themes. Importing replaces all current data — always create a backup first. If a ZIP omits finders.json, existing finders are preserved.
  • Browser import: export bookmarks from Chrome, Firefox, or Edge as an HTML file. A localized preview shows page and bookmark counts before import; folders become categories; duplicate URLs are skipped.
  • CSV export: download all bookmarks as CSV with localized headers (name, URL, category display name, page, shortcut, tags, notes). Opens in Excel or Google Sheets.
config.helpPageBrandingItems:
• Under Essentials → Layout: Layout version (Classic = original look, Modern = refreshed visuals, Glass = translucent blur — same structure), layout preset, density, columns, and dashboard title.
  • Switch layout version from the dashboard command palette: :layoutversion or :layoutversion toggle.
  • Under Advanced → Appearance: background, fonts, and favicon harmonization.
  • Enable auto dark mode to follow system appearance.
  • Upload custom favicon in Advanced → Branding.
  • Upload a custom UI font (.woff/.woff2/.ttf/.otf, max 5 MB) in Advanced → Appearance — it appears as Custom font (uploaded) in the UI font dropdown.
  • Config → theme (desktop): edit custom palettes and packaged built-in themes; export/import JSON; per-session undo; S saves colours; scoped live preview on cards with contrast warning. On phone the tab is read-only — editing needs a wider screen.
  • Theme guided tour: create a temporary Tour demo palette, Save colors, activate on General → Appearance, then remove the demo and restore your previous theme. Replay: System & tools → Show Theme tour again (Theme tab / #colors).
config.helpPageDataItems:
• Server-side data is stored in /data.
  • Device-specific settings are stored in browser local storage.
  • When device-specific mode is enabled, visual behavior can differ between devices.
config.helpPageTroubleshootItems:
• Want the old look back: set Layout version to Classic under Config → General → Layout, or run :layoutversion classic on the dashboard.
  • No bookmarks visible: check page selector and category filter in config.
  • Sorting seems wrong: verify sort mode and pin state.
  • Tips not visible: enable "Show tips above buttons" in Dashboard settings.
  • Search misses items: try fuzzy search and filter syntax (e.g. tag:work).
  • Collections not showing: check config → collections and verify at least one rule has a value.
  • Tag collections empty: ensure bookmarks have tags and the minimum count is not too high.
  • Paste-to-add not working: make sure no input field has focus, search is closed, and "Paste URL to quick-add bookmark" is enabled in config → general → Bookmarks.
  • Quick-add omnibox (&) not responding: make sure no input field has focus and no modal is open. On US keyboards, press Shift+7 for &.
  • New-bookmark modal (+ / Ctrl+Shift+A) not responding: make sure no input field has focus and no other modal is open, or use Ctrl+Shift+A from anywhere.
  • Tag cloud (/ ) missing: desktop or wide layout only — enable Tag cloud (/) in config → general → Header & Buttons.
  • / opens fuzzy search instead of tag cloud: tag cloud only runs on the dashboard when search is closed; inside > search, / is fuzzy (if interleave is on).
config.helpPageTroubleshootFooter: Found a bug or have feedback? Visit the GitHub repository to report issues or suggest improvements.
config.bookmarkDashboardPreviewHint: Hover to see the full tile
config.bookmarkLinkPreviewEmpty: No preview metadata yet — refresh to fetch title, description and image.
config.bookmarkPreviewMaintenanceHint: Refresh or clear title, description and image stored on bookmarks for hover cards and tooltips on the dashboard.
config.bookmarkPreviewMaintenanceInfoMessage:
Each bookmark can store link preview data (title, description, image) used for hover cards and tooltips on the dashboard.

• Refresh all — re-fetches metadata for every bookmark with a URL (may take a while)
• Clear all — removes stored metadata and the server preview cache; previews are fetched again on next hover
• Per-bookmark refresh/clear is also available in Config → Bookmarks
config.bookmarkPreviewRefreshAllConfirmMessage: Re-fetches title, description and image for every bookmark with a URL. This may take a while for large libraries.
config.bookmarkPreviewClearAllConfirmMessage: Removes stored preview title, description and image from every bookmark and clears the server preview cache. Hover cards will fetch again on next use.
config.categoriesIntro:
Categories organise bookmarks within a page. Select a page to manage its categories.
Drag the ⠿ handle to reorder (saves automatically). Merge combines two categories and moves their bookmarks.
config.categoriesListEmptyHint: No categories on this page yet. Add one to organise bookmarks.
config.categoriesMobileOnlyDesktop: Category management is available on desktop. Open config on a larger screen to add or reorder categories.
config.categoryNameMustBeUnique: Category name must be unique and not empty.
config.mergeCategoryImpact: {count} bookmarks will move to the target category.
config.findersIntro: A finder is a shortcut to a search engine. Set a search URL with %s where your query should go (e.g. https://www.google.com/search?q=%s), pick a short letter shortcut, and on the dashboard type ? plus that shortcut and your words — e.g. ?du linux opens DuckDuckGo with “linux” in your browser.
config.pagesIntro:
Pages group your bookmarks. Each page has its own set of categories and bookmarks on the dashboard.
Drag the ⠿ handle to reorder pages (saves automatically). Use Archive to hide a page without deleting its bookmarks. Double-click a page tab on the dashboard to rename it.
config.pagesMobileOnlyDesktop: Page management is available on desktop. Open config on a larger screen to add or reorder pages.
config.dashboardSyncFailed: Dashboard sync failed. Retry from config.
config.tagsTabIntro: Manage tags across all bookmarks. Rename or delete tags globally, or see which bookmarks carry each tag. Changes save automatically.
config.tagsListEmptyHint: No tags yet. Add tags to bookmarks via the Bookmarks tab or the inline editor on the dashboard.
config.tagsMobileOnlyDesktop: Tag management is available on desktop. Open config on a larger screen to rename, merge, or delete tags.
config.tagMergeMessage: Tag "{new}" already exists on {count} bookmarks. Merge "{old}" into it?
config.tagDeleteMessage: Removes the tag from {count} bookmarks. Bookmarks are kept.
config.featureTourHint: Start the interactive tour: learn search, finders, commands and key settings.
config.themeInfoMessage:
Chooses the colour theme for the dashboard and config.

• Includes built-in dark/light and any custom themes from Config → theme
• Saved when you click Save in config
config.autoDarkModeInfoMessage:
Automatically switches between light and dark theme based on your system preference.

• Only works with built-in themes that have dark and light variants
• Not available with custom themes — those use one fixed palette
• Useful on laptops and phones that follow OS appearance
config.autoDarkModeUnavailableHint: Not available with custom themes. Custom themes use one fixed palette instead of separate dark and light variants. Select a built-in theme to enable auto dark mode.
config.systemAppearanceHintActive: Auto dark mode is on — the dashboard theme follows this system appearance.
config.systemAppearanceHintIdle: Your OS appearance right now. Enable auto dark mode to switch themes when this changes.
config.systemAppearanceHintUnsupported: System appearance shown for reference. Auto dark mode needs a built-in dark/light theme pair — not available with custom themes.
config.backgroundPickerInfoMessage:
Optional wallpaper behind the bookmark grid.

• None: plain theme background
• Auto: gradient matched to the active theme
• Gradient / Image: pick a preset or paste an image URL
• Opacity slider controls how strong it appears
config.backgroundOpacityInfoMessage:
How visible the background is (65–100%).

• Lower values keep bookmarks easier to read
• Applies to gradient and image backgrounds
config.showBackgroundDotsInfoMessage:
Subtle dot pattern on the dashboard background.

• Purely decorative
• Turn off for a cleaner look
config.enableAnimationsInfoMessage:
UI transitions and motion effects.

• On: smoother category collapse, modals, etc.
• Off: snappier feel, can help on slower devices
config.fontPresetInfoMessage:
Font family for the whole interface.

• Mono fonts suit the terminal aesthetic
• Sans fonts are easier for long reading
• Upload a custom font below — it appears as an option in this dropdown and stays available when you switch presets
config.fontSizeInfoMessage:
Global text scale from xs to xl.

• Affects bookmarks, config, and search
• Combine with density for tighter layouts
config.fontWeightInfoMessage:
How bold body text appears.

• Normal is default

config.iconStylingInfoMessage:
Tints bookmark favicons to match the active theme.

• Muted / Tinted / Overlay styles
• Intensity slider controls strength
• Preview shows sample icons
config.columnsInfoMessage:
How many bookmark tiles fit on one row (1–6).

• Wider screens often suit 3–4

config.layoutVersionInfoMessage:
Switch between classic, modern, and glass dashboard styling.

• Classic: current look, unchanged
• Modern: updated visuals, same structure
• Glass: translucent iOS-style surfaces with blur
• Themes still control all colors
config.layoutPresetInfoMessage:
Overall bookmark grid style.

• Default, Compact, Cards, Masonry, List, Launcher, etc.
• Each changes spacing, card shape, and row height
config.densityModeInfoMessage:
Spacing between tiles and text size within the preset.

• Comfortable → Dense → Auto
• Auto adapts to screen size and zoom
config.showDashboardTitleInfoMessage:
Shows the nextDash title (or custom title) at the top.

• Off: more vertical space for bookmarks
config.launcherIconSizeInfoMessage:
Icon scale when using the Launcher layout preset.

• Only applies in Launcher mode
config.calendarUrlInfoMessage:
Link opened when you use the calendar shortcut from the date line.

• Example: Google Calendar, Outlook web
• Leave empty to disable
config.showIconsInfoMessage:
Shows favicon or custom icon on each bookmark.

• Fetched automatically when adding links
• Can be refreshed from config → bookmarks
config.showShortcutsInfoMessage:
Displays keyboard shortcut labels on tiles.

• Used with / or letter search depending on search mode
• Global shortcuts setting affects cross-page use
config.showPinIconInfoMessage:
Small pin marker on pinned bookmarks.

• Pin via command :pin or inline edit
config.showNoteIconInfoMessage:
Indicator when a bookmark has a note.

• Notes are edited with :note or inline edit
config.showLinkPreviewCardsInfoMessage:
Hover card with title/description preview for a bookmark.

• Only on keyboard focus or hover
• Delay setting avoids accidental popups
config.linkPreviewHoverDelayInfoMessage:
How long to wait before showing the preview card.

• Fast (100ms), Balanced (150ms), Calm (250ms)
config.bookmarkSortingInfoMessage:
Default order for bookmarks on each page.

• Manual: drag order
• A–Z, Recently used, Pinned first
config.openLinksInNewTabInfoMessage:
Opens bookmark URLs in a new browser tab.

config.pasteUrlQuickAddInfoMessage:
Paste a URL on the dashboard to open the new-bookmark flow.

• Works when no input field is focused
• Ctrl+V on dashboard
config.languageInfoMessage:
Interface language for dashboard, config, and modals.

• Applies immediately in config
• Extension popup follows its own locale rules
config.showDateInfoMessage:
Date line in the dashboard header.

• Format chosen below when enabled
config.dateFormatInfoMessage:
How the date is formatted.

• Examples shown in the dropdown

config.showTimeInfoMessage:
Clock in the dashboard header.

• 12h or 24h format below
config.showWeatherWithDateInfoMessage:
Shows temperature (and conditions when available) beside the date.

• Requires location settings below
config.weatherSourceInfoMessage:
How location is determined.

config.weatherLocationInfoMessage:
City or place name for manual weather lookup.

config.weatherUnitInfoMessage: Celsius or Fahrenheit for displayed temperature.
config.weatherRefreshInfoMessage:
How often to fetch new weather data.

config.enableSmartCollectionsInfoMessage:
Automatic categories such as Today, Recently opened, or Stale.

config.buttonBarPositionInfoMessage:
Where the footer button bar sits.

config.showDockLayoutSelectorInfoMessage:
Shows a layout switcher in the footer dock.

config.colorizeStatusInfoMessage:

config.showPingTimesInfoMessage:

config.showStatusLoadingInfoMessage:

config.deviceSpecificSettingsInfoMessage:

config.enableCustomFaviconInfoMessage:

config.enableCustomTitleInfoMessage:

config.helpPageConfigGeneralItems:
• Opaque chrome (v2026.06.21): Save row and main tab bar use a solid background so scrolling panels do not show through the buttons. In Advanced and All, the layer toolbar and section nav stay sticky while scrolling.
  • Phone vs tablet: Config limits to General + Help only on phones (≤768px). Portrait tablets and wider touch layouts keep the full config, Essentials/Advanced layers, and guided tours; phone General orders panels language → theme → layout.
  • Essentials / Advanced / All: Everyday options (language, appearance, layout, bookmarks, smart collections, and a compact status monitoring overview with monitored bookmark count and a Health link) live under Essentials. Power features (full status tuning, branding, search input, system tools) are under Advanced. All shows every panel on one scrollable page with Expand all / Collapse all. Panels collapse/expand (state is remembered); sticky section nav jumps between cards; hash links like #general/advanced/layout open the right layer and panel. Many controls have a ↺ reset to default button.
  • ℹ info buttons: Click the small ℹ next to a setting label for a short explanation in your current language.
  • After Save: a success toast offers Open dashboard — layout and visual changes apply when you return; pending sync is applied automatically via session storage.
  • Guided config tours: On a desktop-width window, the first visit to each config tab can start a spotlight tour: General (overview-only), Bookmarks (extended, with optional demo bookmarks), Pages, Categories, Tags, Collections, Finders (optional Google example), Stats, and Theme (demo custom palette → General → Appearance → cleanup). Tours do not run on mobile; rotating tips and promo banners are hidden there too. Each tour runs once until finished or skipped; completion syncs to settings and localStorage. Replay: Advanced → System & tools — Show … tour again for each tab (open that tab first). See also Help sections for Bookmarks, Finders, Tags, Collections, Categories, Pages (under Manage), Stats (under Manage), and Theme (under Branding).
  • Branding & PWA: Custom title and favicon (Advanced → Branding) apply to the browser tab, /manifest.webmanifest, and installed home-screen apps.
  • Find settings (desktop): Search settings… in the breadcrumb bar — Ctrl+Shift+K / Cmd+Shift+K — jumps to any tab, General panel, label, stats section, or Help block; finds Advanced panels even while Essentials is active. Quick actions — Ctrl+K / Cmd+K — runs save, open dashboard, and tour-reset actions only (not settings navigation). A one-time settings search promo (pulsing field and balloon) may appear on first desktop visit until dismissed.
  • Post-onboarding & resets: What's new may open when unread; classic users may see a layout-versions tip and paste spotlight (separate hints, no queue). Tours & onboarding (Advanced → System & tools): Reset layout versions prompt, Reset paste spotlight, Reset settings search promo, and per-tab tour buttons.
  • Browser extension: Load the extension from the extension/ folder in your nextDash install, point it at your server URL, and save tabs as bookmarks. When the dashboard is open, saves can show a toast and refresh bookmarks automatically.
  • Re-run setup: Config → General → Advanced → System & tools → Show onboarding wizard again (runs on the dashboard).

colors.palettesInfoMessage:
Three ways to edit colors on this tab:

• Dark and Light — change the fallback palettes for the classic dark/light themes in General → Appearance.

• Custom themes — create your own single-palette themes with Add Custom Theme. Each custom theme is one fixed look, not a day/night pair.

• Built-in named themes (Cherry Graphite, Nordic Frost, etc.) are picked in General → Appearance. Their packaged colors live in the server defaults unless you override palettes here.
colors.saveColorsInfoMessage:
Two separate save actions:

• Save colors (this tab) — writes palette edits from the Theme tab to the server. Use this after changing hex values or adding/removing custom themes.

• Save (config header) — stores General settings: which theme is active, layout, bookmarks, language, etc. It does not save color hex values from this tab.

Typical flow: edit colors → Save colors → pick the theme under General → Appearance → Save in the header.
colors.customThemesInfoMessage:
Custom themes are single palettes you create here.

• Add Custom Theme clones the default starter colors. Rename the theme and adjust colors in the editor on the right.

• To use it on the dashboard, select it under General → Appearance and click Save in the config header.

• Auto dark mode (General → Appearance) only works with built-in themes that have separate dark and light variants. It is disabled while a custom theme is selected — custom themes do not switch with your system appearance.
